CHT with the method of nonequilibrium internal oxidation, similarly to the works in [25,32,33], consisted of two stages: (1) formation of a surface scale during annealing in air at 650◦C for 5 to 30 min
and (2) vacuum annealing with a total duration of 9 h, with a stepwise increase in temperature from 620 to 1000◦C, to transfer oxygen from the surface scale into the sample.

attributes.size: near surface: 5–10 µm wide, several hundred µm long; 200 µm depth: 10–15 µm wide, 50–150 µm long; 250–300 µm depth: 25–30 µm wide, ≤100 µm long

evidence.quote: Near the surface, the grains were 5 to 10µm wide, while they were several hundredµm long. At a distance of 200µm from the surface, the width of the grains varied from 10 to 15µm, and their length was 50–150µm. At a distance of 250–300µm from the surface, the grain width could reach 25–30µm.

attributes.size: near surface (≤150 µm): 10–30 µm wide, 150–200 µm long; ≥175 µm depth: 25–30 µm wide, ~150 µm long; central (≥400 µm): up to 40 µm wide, ≤100 µm long

evidence.quote: The grain width in this region increased, compared to annealing at 1000◦C (Figure 1a), and it was from 10 to 30µm, while the grain length was 150–200µm. At distances from the surface of ~175µm or more, grains 25–30µm wide and about 150µm long were predominantly observed.
